queue.title: Spec loop R1 -- explore and propose
queue.detail: The drain count is 0, so the spec loop runs. D-1's drive produced a defect, and by this item's own priority order that outranks an open ledger finding and outranks any research candidate. SPEC F309 AND F310 TOGETHER -- same screen, same keystroke, same fix surface, and F310's fix shape changes what F309's can be. F309 (A): choosing 'Move to blocked' on a ticket mounts the mandatory reason input with autoFocus, and autoFocus loses -- RowMenu's Radix DropdownMenu returns focus to its trigger as it closes, after React mounted the input. Measured: activeElement is BUTTON task-status-menu-<id>, the field holds '' after 19 keystrokes, and because the trigger is a <button> every SPACE in the typed reason re-opens the menu and makes the page inert. The mouse path works, so it is a focus defect, not a broken control. F310 (B): useDialogFocus binds Escape on document and never asks whether something nearer handled it, so Escape closes the menu AND the ticket, and Escape in the reason input cancels the reason AND closes the ticket -- meaning TaskDetailDrawer.tsx:413-414 has never once been observable. BEFORE PROPOSING: F310's fix touches a hook serving SIX call sites (grep -rn useDialogFocus hub/ui/src --include=*.tsx; F307's table lists only five -- see F311), and F307 is an OPEN finding against the Tab branch of the same hook, so read F307 and decide explicitly whether this proposal subsumes it or deliberately leaves it. Reproductions: scripts/drive/t_d1_0910_escape_across_the_dialogs.py (30 pass / 6 fail) and scripts/drive/t_d1_0910_rowmenu_leaves_the_page_inert.py (18 pass / 1 fail); both assert in the direction of correct behaviour, so they go green when this ships. Write openspec/changes/<name>/ with proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md and specs/<capability>/spec.md deltas. `openspec new change` refuses a name starting with a digit. `openspec validate --strict <name>` must pass, and it reads only a requirement's FIRST PHYSICAL LINE for the modal, so SHALL goes on line 1. Specs live in openspec, never also in the Hub. F292's next instrument remains a strong candidate for a LATER loop -- see the iteration 2 log entry -- but it is an instrument change, not a product defect, and F309 is a product defect an operator hits on a mandatory path.
